lines.trans: Aha! Behold this quiet historic wall—we must be right behind the clock square!
Good morning again, boss! Did you forget your wallet, or did you miss me?
Rocio?! Why are you standing inside a window behind the municipal clock tower?!
Because three left turns make a circle, Ernesto, and this is our own kitchen window!

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: Wait—tell me you took your famous back-alley shortcut without your glasses again!
Someone clearly moved that green garden fence since last spring!
Look on the bright side: nobody gets hungry on a circular expedition!
Here, take three warm cinnamon rolls in a paper bag before you try again.
Thank you, Rocio, and please do not mention a single word of this to Mateo.
My lips are sealed, provided you follow Javier and the brass compass from here!

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
always (siempre que = whenever / as long as)

Very well, walk straight up Calle de los Tilos—I was merely testing your sense of direction!
Aha! Behold this quiet historic wall—we must be right behind the clock square!

To miss someone.

Aha! Behold this quiet historic wall—we must be right behind the clock square!

always (siempre que = whenever / as long as)

lines.trans: Deal! Hand over command of the map cards, Ernesto, before twelve noon strikes!
Very well, walk straight up Calle de los Tilos—I was merely testing your sense of direction!
See you!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Exclamation of discovery or agreement.

examples.text: ¡Ajá, aquí estaban mis gafas!
examples.trans: Aha, here were my glasses!

examples.text: Ajá, eso explica el ruido.
examples.trans: Aha, that explains the noise.

meanings.note: Refers exclusively to people.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de llamar a la puerta.
examples.trans: Someone just knocked at the door.

examples.text: ¿Hay alguien en recepción?
examples.trans: Is anyone at the front desk?

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.text: Llegué diez minutos antes.
examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.text: Aquí tiene su llave.
examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

asomar.gloss: to peek out; to stick out

meanings.en: to peek out; to stick out
meanings.note: Describes something peeking from a window, pocket, or hinge.

examples.text: Un papel blanco asoma del sobre.
examples.trans: A white sheet peeks out of the envelope.

examples.text: El sol ya asoma por los tejados.
examples.trans: The sun is already peeking over the roofs.

meanings.note: Commonly paired with tomar ('to take a shortcut': tomar un atajo).

examples.text: Ernesto conoce un atajo rápido por el callejón.
examples.trans: Ernesto knows a quick shortcut down the alley.

examples.text: Si tomamos este atajo, llegaremos antes del mediodía.
examples.trans: If we take this shortcut, we will arrive before noon.

meanings.note: Before an adjective (bien caliente), means 'nice and hot'.

examples.text: Todo va muy bien hoy.
examples.trans: Everything is going very well today.

examples.text: El té sale bien caliente.
examples.trans: The tea comes out nice and hot.

meanings.note: Shopping or paper/cloth bag.

examples.text: La bolsa está aquí.
examples.trans: The bag is here.

examples.text: Vemos las bolsas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bags from the door.

meanings.note: Specifically a magnetic pocket or ship's compass; a drawing compass with two legs is un compás.

examples.text: Dentro de la bolsa había una brújula antigua de latón.
examples.trans: Inside the pouch was an old brass compass.

examples.text: Un buen cartógrafo nunca viaja sin su brújula.
examples.trans: A good mapmaker never travels without his compass.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.text: ¡Buenos días a todos!
examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!

examples.text: Hace muy buen tiempo hoy.
examples.trans: The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: Describes hot drinks, food, or water.

examples.text: Es una pieza caliente.
examples.trans: It is a hot piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene, señora: té caliente de menta con miel.
examples.trans: Here you are, madam: hot mint tea with honey.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la calle.

examples.text: La calle está aquí.
examples.trans: The street is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the streets from the door.

meanings.note: Plural callejones.

examples.text: El callejón está aquí.
examples.trans: The alley is here.

examples.text: Vemos los callejones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the alleys from the door.

meanings.note: Fragrant baking spice.

examples.text: La canela es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The cinnamon is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la canela.
examples.trans: We talk about the cinnamon.

meanings.note: Everyday word in Spain for a pocket wallet or cardholder, as well as a leather satchel.

examples.text: ¿Se ha olvidado usted la cartera en la cocina, jefe?
examples.trans: Did you forget your wallet in the kitchen, boss?

examples.text: Guardé la postal doblada dentro de mi cartera.
examples.trans: I kept the folded postcard inside my wallet.

meanings.note: Invariable for masculine and feminine in the singular; plural adds -es (circulares).

examples.text: Nadie pasa hambre en una expedición circular por el barrio.
examples.trans: Nobody goes hungry on a circular expedition through the neighbourhood.

examples.text: Colocaron una mesa circular en el centro de la galería.
examples.trans: They placed a circular table in the middle of the sunroom.

examples.text: Mi destino está claramente trazado.
examples.trans: My destiny is clearly mapped out.

examples.text: Yo claramente
examples.trans: I claramente

meanings.note: Both the kitchen room and the stove/cuisine.

examples.text: La cocina está aquí.
examples.trans: The kitchen is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cocinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the kitchens from the door.

contemplar.gloss: to behold; to gaze at; to contemplate

meanings.en: to behold; to gaze at; to contemplate
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb used for admiring a view, building, or work of art calmly.

examples.text: Contemplad este tranquilo muro histórico detrás de la plaza.
examples.trans: Behold this quiet historic wall behind the square.

examples.text: Nos quedamos en el balcón contemplando las luces del patio.
examples.trans: We stayed on the balcony gazing at the courtyard lights.

meanings.note: Always keeps its written accent on the first syllable (el círculo, los círculos).

examples.text: Tres giros a la izquierda hacen un círculo completo.
examples.trans: Three left turns make a complete circle.

examples.text: Sentémonos en círculo alrededor de la mesa baja del jardín.
examples.trans: Let us sit in a circle around the low garden table.

dar.gloss: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)

meanings.en: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg doy and preterite di/dio; dar las doce = strike twelve.

examples.text: La ventana da al patio soleado.
examples.trans: The window looks out onto the sunny courtyard.

examples.text: El reloj acaba de dar las doce.
examples.trans: The clock has just struck twelve.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: With a noun object (le debo la verdad), means 'to owe'; before an infinitive, means 'should / ought to'.

examples.text: Le debo diez euros de cambio.
examples.trans: I owe you ten euros in change.

examples.text: Todo funciona como debe ser.
examples.trans: Everything works as it should.

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.text: ¿Qué dice la carta exactamente?
examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?

examples.text: Dime la verdad sin miedo.
examples.trans: Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Marks a starting point in space or time.

examples.text: No hablamos desde aquel domingo.
examples.trans: We have not spoken since that Sunday.

examples.text: Abrimos al público desde mañana.
examples.trans: We open to the public starting tomorrow.

meanings.note: Detrás de + noun means 'behind something'.

examples.text: El jardín está detrás de la casa.
examples.trans: The garden is behind the house.

examples.text: Hay otra página detrás del aviso.
examples.trans: There is another page behind the notice.

meanings.note: Las doce = twelve o'clock.

examples.text: El reloj da las doce al mediodía.
examples.trans: The clock strikes twelve at noon.

examples.text: Aquí tienes doce euros de cambio.
examples.trans: Here is twelve euros in change.

meanings.note: Masculine despite ending in -a: el día, ¡Buenos días!.

examples.text: El día está aquí.
examples.trans: The day is here.

examples.text: Vemos los días desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the days from the door.

echar.gloss: to pour; to toss; to miss (echar de menos)

meanings.en: to pour; to toss; to miss (echar de menos)
meanings.note: Echar un vistazo = take a glance; echar de menos = miss someone.

examples.text: Echa un poco más de agua caliente.
examples.trans: Pour a little more hot water.

examples.text: Te he echado mucho de menos.
examples.trans: I have missed you very much.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells g -> gu: entregué.

examples.text: Entrego el paquete en recepción.
examples.trans: I hand the parcel over at reception.

examples.text: El cartero entregó una carta urgente.
examples.trans: The postman delivered an urgent letter.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.text: Pásame ese cuaderno azul.
examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.text: Espere un momento, por favor.
examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.

examples.text: Esperamos que descanse muy bien.
examples.trans: We hope you rest very well.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.text: El desayuno ya está listo.
examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.

examples.text: ¿Dónde están las llaves de latón?
examples.trans: Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.text: Este patio es muy tranquilo.
examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.

examples.text: Esta mañana hace mucho sol.
examples.trans: This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Neuter pronoun used when not naming a gendered noun.

examples.text: He encontrado esto en el sótano.
examples.trans: I found this in the cellar.

examples.text: ¿Qué es esto encima de la mesa?
examples.trans: What is this on top of the table?

meanings.note: Drops its written accent in the plural: las expediciones.

examples.text: Javier apunta cada giro de nuestra expedición en su cuaderno.
examples.trans: Javier writes down every turn of our expedition in his notebook.

examples.text: Prepararon bocadillos y agua fresca para la expedición del sábado.
examples.trans: They packed sandwiches and cool water for the Saturday outing.

meanings.note: Can stand before the noun when referring to something ironically or affectionately well-known (tu famoso atajo).

examples.text: Ernesto volvió a tomar su famoso atajo por el callejón.
examples.trans: Ernesto took his famous back-alley shortcut again.

examples.text: El huésped quiere probar el famoso pastel de almendra de la posada.
examples.trans: The guest wants to taste the inn's famous almond cake.

meanings.note: Por favor literally means 'as a favour'.

examples.text: El favor está aquí.
examples.trans: The favour is here.

examples.text: Vemos los favores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the favours from the door.

meanings.note: Plural-only feminine noun in Spain: las gafas.

examples.text: ¿Dónde he dejado mis gafas?
examples.trans: Where did I leave my glasses?

examples.text: Lleva unas gafas redondas.
examples.trans: He wears round glasses.

examples.text: A ver un giro.
examples.trans: Let's see a twirl.

examples.text: Haz un giro despacio.
examples.trans: Do a slow twirl.

meanings.note: Gracias por + noun/infinitive expresses 'thank you for...'.

examples.text: ¡Muchas gracias por su ayuda!
examples.trans: Thank you very much for your help!

examples.text: Gracias por venir hoy.
examples.trans: Thank you for coming today.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.

examples.text: Ya hemos preparado las habitaciones.
examples.trans: We have already prepared the rooms.

hacer.gloss: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)

meanings.en: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)
meanings.note: Irregular: hago, hice, hecho; hace tres años = three years ago.

examples.text: La panadera hace pan fresco cada mañana.
examples.trans: The baker bakes fresh bread every morning.

examples.text: Llegó hace diez minutos.
examples.trans: She arrived ten minutes ago.

meanings.note: Feminine noun taking el in singular when article is used (tengo mucha hambre).

examples.text: El hambre es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The hunger is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el hambre.
examples.trans: We talk about the hunger.

meanings.note: Irregular past participle of hacer (recién hecho = freshly made).

examples.text: Es una pieza hecha.
examples.trans: It is a made piece.

examples.text: ¡Son bollos recién hechos! Toma uno, todavía está caliente.
examples.trans: They are freshly baked rolls! Take one, it is still warm.

meanings.note: Describes heritage buildings and old quarters.

examples.text: Es una pieza histórica.
examples.trans: It is a historic piece.

examples.text: ¡Un arquitecto que trabaja con patios históricos por toda Valencia!
examples.trans: An architect who works with historic courtyard buildings all over Valencia!

meanings.note: Followed directly by an infinitive (intenté sonreír).

examples.text: Intento aprender diez palabras al día.
examples.trans: I try to learn ten words a day.

examples.text: Intenté llamarte ayer por la tarde.
examples.trans: I tried calling you yesterday afternoon.

meanings.note: A la izquierda = on/to the left.

examples.text: La izquierda está aquí.
examples.trans: The left is here.

examples.text: Vemos las izquierdas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lefts from the door.

meanings.note: Plural jardines, without the written accent.

examples.text: Mi madre tiene flores en el jardín.
examples.trans: My mother has flowers in the garden.

examples.text: Los niños juegan en el jardín.
examples.trans: The children play in the garden.

meanings.note: Feminine: la jefa.

examples.text: El jefe está aquí.
examples.trans: The boss is here.

examples.text: Vemos los jefes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bosss from the door.

meanings.note: Justo aquí = right here; justo al lado = right next door.

examples.text: La llave está justo aquí.
examples.trans: The key is right here.

examples.text: La panadería queda justo al lado.
examples.trans: The bakery is right next door.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Al lado = on the side / next door.

examples.text: El lado está aquí.
examples.trans: The side is here.

examples.text: Vemos los lados desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sides from the door.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.text: Las ventanas dan al jardín.
examples.trans: The windows face the garden.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las ocho.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Yellow copper-zinc alloy used for keys, lamps, and valves.

examples.text: El latón es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The brass is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el latón.
examples.trans: We talk about the brass.

meanings.note: Third-person singular indirect object pronoun.

examples.text: Le llevo una taza de té caliente.
examples.trans: I am bringing you/her a cup of hot tea.

examples.text: ¿Le gusta la habitación del patio?
examples.trans: Do you like the courtyard room?

llevar.gloss: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)

meanings.en: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)
meanings.note: Versatile verb for carrying items, wearing clothes/glasses, or duration.

examples.text: Llevo dos tazas calientes al jardín.
examples.trans: I carry two hot cups to the garden.

examples.text: Hoy lleva un abrigo gris oscuro.
examples.trans: Today he is wearing a dark grey coat.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.text: Los vecinos vienen a desayunar.
examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: Derived from mandar ('to command/send'); entregar el mando means 'to hand over command'.

examples.text: Entregue usted el mando de las tarjetas del mapa, Ernesto.
examples.trans: Hand over command of the map cards, Ernesto.

examples.text: Clara tomó el mando de la expedición con la brújula en la mano.
examples.trans: Clara took command of the expedition with the compass in her hand.

meanings.note: Masculine noun despite ending in -a: el mapa antiguo, estos mapas mojados.

examples.text: Mateo dibujó un mapa sencillo para llegar a la ferretería.
examples.trans: Mateo drew a simple map to get to the hardware shop.

examples.text: Extendimos el mapa de Valencia sobre la mesa de madera.
examples.trans: We spread the map of Valencia out on the wooden table.

meanings.note: First-person singular object/reflexive pronoun.

examples.text: ¿Me pasas la sal, por favor?
examples.trans: Can you pass me the salt, please?

examples.text: Vivo aquí y trabajo aquí.
examples.trans: I live here and I work here.

meanings.note: Al mediodía = at noon.

examples.text: El mediodía es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The noon is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el mediodía.
examples.trans: We talk about the noon.

meanings.note: Por lo menos = at least; echar de menos = to miss; a menos que = unless.

examples.text: Son las ocho menos diez.
examples.trans: It is ten to eight.

examples.text: Por lo menos ya no llueve.
examples.trans: At least it is no longer raining.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: muevo).

examples.text: Movemos la mesa bajo la sombra.
examples.trans: We move the table into the shade.

examples.text: El viento suave movió las hojas.
examples.trans: The gentle breeze stirred the leaves.

meanings.note: Plural municipales.

examples.text: Es una pieza municipal.
examples.trans: It is a municipal piece.

examples.text: Bien pensado, Clara. Javier lee normas municipales de edificios cada semana.
examples.trans: Smart thinking, Clara. Javier reads city building rules every single week.

meanings.note: Exterior or structural masonry wall.

examples.text: El muro está aquí.
examples.trans: The thick wall is here.

examples.text: Vemos los muros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the thick walls from the door.

meanings.note: Shortened form of mucho used before adjectives and adverbs.

examples.text: El bizcocho está muy rico.
examples.trans: The sponge cake is very tasty.

examples.text: Camina muy rápido por el puente.
examples.trans: She walks very fast across the bridge.

meanings.note: Requires no before the verb when nadie follows (no hay nadie).

examples.text: Todavía no hay nadie en el patio.
examples.trans: There is nobody in the courtyard yet.

examples.text: Nadie conoce mejor este edificio.
examples.trans: Nobody knows this building better.

meanings.note: Ni... ni... = neither... nor...; ni una gota = not a single drop.

examples.text: No cae ni una sola gota.
examples.trans: Not a single drop is falling.

examples.text: No tengo ni papel ni bolígrafo.
examples.trans: I have neither paper nor pen.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.text: Hoy no llueve en Valencia.
examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

nos.gloss: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)

meanings.en: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)
meanings.note: First-person plural object/reflexive/reciprocal pronoun.

examples.text: ¡Nos vemos mañana por la mañana!
examples.trans: See you tomorrow morning!

examples.text: Nos alegra mucho la noticia.
examples.trans: The news makes us very glad.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.text: Nuestra posada tiene ocho habitaciones.
examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.

examples.text: Nuestros vecinos toman café aquí.
examples.trans: Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Becomes u before words starting with o- or ho-.

examples.text: ¿Prefieres café o té caliente?
examples.trans: Do you prefer coffee or hot tea?

examples.text: ¿Abrimos hoy o esperamos a mañana?
examples.trans: Do we open today or wait until tomorrow?

meanings.note: Used directly (olvidé la llave) or pronominally with de (me olvidé de...).

examples.text: Nunca olvido una cara amable.
examples.trans: I never forget a friendly face.

examples.text: Olvidé mi paraguas junto al mostrador.
examples.trans: I left my umbrella beside the counter.

meanings.note: Paired with sentido in el sentido de la orientación ('sense of direction').

examples.text: Solo ponía a prueba vuestro sentido de la orientación.
examples.trans: I was merely testing your sense of direction.

examples.text: Gracias a la orientación sur, la galería recibe sol todo el día.
examples.trans: Thanks to its southern orientation, the sunroom gets sun all day.

meanings.note: Spanish never puts un/una before otro (otra taza = another cup; otra vez = again).

examples.text: ¿Quiere otra taza de café?
examples.trans: Would you like another cup of coffee?

examples.text: Míralo otra vez a la luz.
examples.trans: Look at it again in the light.

meanings.note: Ni una palabra = not a word.

examples.text: La palabra está aquí.
examples.trans: The word is here.

examples.text: Vemos las palabras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the words from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los papeles.

examples.text: El papel está aquí.
examples.trans: The paper is here.

examples.text: Vemos los papeles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the papers from the door.

pasado.gloss: last; past (la semana pasada = last week)

meanings.en: last; past (la semana pasada = last week)
meanings.note: Agrees with its noun.

examples.text: Es una pieza pasada.
examples.trans: It is a last piece.

examples.text: Bombilla nueva la semana pasada, jabón limpio y mucha agua caliente.
examples.trans: New bulb last week, clean soap, and plenty of hot water.

pasar.gloss: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen

meanings.en: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen
meanings.note: ¿Qué pasa? = What's wrong?; No pasa nada = No problem.

examples.text: ¡Pase, por favor, y siéntese!
examples.trans: Come in, please, and have a seat!

examples.text: Pasa la farmacia verde a la derecha.
examples.trans: Pass the green pharmacy on your right.

meanings.note: Public town square, often hosting neighbourhood stalls on weekend mornings.

examples.text: Hay puestos de fruta fresca en la plaza del barrio.
examples.trans: There are fresh fruit stalls in the neighbourhood square.

examples.text: Cruzamos la plaza soleada con dos cestas.
examples.trans: We cross the sunny square with two baskets.

poner.gloss: to put; to set; to become (ponerse + adj)

meanings.en: to put; to set; to become (ponerse + adj)
meanings.note: Irregular: pongo, pon, puse, puesto; ponerse nervioso = get nervous.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas limpias en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two clean cups on the table.

examples.text: Pon la maleta junto al mostrador.
examples.trans: Set the suitcase beside the counter.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.text: Paseamos por el casco antiguo.
examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: One word without accent (distinct from ¿por qué? = why?).

examples.text: Abro la ventana porque hace calor.
examples.trans: I open the window because it is warm.

examples.text: Sonríe porque huele a canela.
examples.trans: She smiles because it smells of cinnamon.

meanings.note: Seasons take the article: en primavera, la primavera.

examples.text: En primavera hay flores en todas partes.
examples.trans: In spring there are flowers everywhere.

examples.text: La primavera en Valencia es muy agradable.
examples.trans: Spring in Valencia is very pleasant.

probar.gloss: to try; to taste; to test

meanings.en: to try; to taste; to test
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: pruebo).

examples.text: Prueba este pan con aceite de oliva.
examples.trans: Try this bread with olive oil.

examples.text: Ayer probamos la mermelada de manzana.
examples.trans: Yesterday we tasted the apple jam.

meanings.note: Mi propia maleta = my own suitcase.

examples.text: Es una pieza propia.
examples.trans: It is an own piece.

examples.text: ¿Y no pidió su propia maleta con el tren de madera?
examples.trans: And he did not ask for his own suitcase with the wooden train?

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.text: Espero que descanses muy bien.
examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.text: ¿Qué hora es ahora mismo?
examples.trans: What time is it right now?

examples.text: ¡Qué mañana tan luminosa!
examples.trans: What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Sigue todo recto = go straight ahead.

examples.text: Es una pieza recta.
examples.trans: It is a straight piece.

examples.text: A la izquierda en la puerta, todo recto hasta el puente. ¿Cruzo el río?
examples.trans: Left at the gate, straight ahead to the bridge. Do I cross the river?

meanings.note: Covers wristwatches, wall clocks, and church tower clocks (plural: relojes).

examples.text: El reloj está aquí.
examples.trans: The watch is here.

examples.text: Vemos los relojes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the watchs from the door.

meanings.note: Baked pastry roll or scroll.

examples.text: El rollo está aquí.
examples.trans: The roll is here.

examples.text: Vemos los rollos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rolls from the door.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.text: La puerta se abre despacio.
examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

seguir.gloss: to continue; to keep (doing); to go straight (seguir recto)

meanings.en: to continue; to keep (doing); to go straight (seguir recto)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: sigo, sigue, siguió); seguir + gerund = keep doing.

examples.text: Sigue todo recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead to the bridge.

examples.text: ¿El agua sigue caliente?
examples.trans: Is the water still hot?

meanings.note: Covers the five senses, common sense (sentido común), sense of direction (sentido de la orientación), and way of traffic.

examples.text: Ernesto decía que solo ponía a prueba nuestro sentido de la orientación.
examples.trans: Ernesto claimed he was only testing our sense of direction.

examples.text: Esta calle estrecha es de un solo sentido para los autobuses.
examples.trans: This narrow street is one-way for buses.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.

examples.text: Esa maleta azul es mía.
examples.trans: That blue suitcase is mine.

siempre.gloss: always (siempre que = whenever / as long as)

meanings.en: always (siempre que = whenever / as long as)
meanings.note: Opposite of nunca.

examples.text: El patio siempre está tranquilo.
examples.trans: The courtyard is always quiet.

examples.text: Ven siempre que quieras tomar café.
examples.trans: Come whenever you want to have coffee.

meanings.note: Followed by bare nouns (sin azúcar, sin sal) or infinitives (sin abrir = unopened).

examples.text: Tomo el té sin azúcar, gracias.
examples.trans: I take my tea without sugar, thank you.

examples.text: Salió de casa sin abrigo.
examples.trans: He left home without a coat.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.text: Solo necesito cinco minutos más.
examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.

examples.text: Queda una sola habitación libre.
examples.trans: Only a single room remains vacant.

subir.gloss: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs

meanings.en: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs
meanings.note: Works both intransitively and transitively.

examples.text: Subo las toallas limpias a la primera planta.
examples.trans: I carry the clean towels up to the first floor.

examples.text: Subieron despacio la escalera de madera.
examples.trans: They climbed the wooden stairs slowly.

meanings.note: Pagar con tarjeta = pay by card.

examples.text: La tarjeta está aquí.
examples.trans: The card is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tarjetas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cards from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Toma! = Here you go!; tomar un café = have a coffee.

examples.text: ¿Qué quiere tomar para desayunar?
examples.trans: What would you like to have for breakfast?

examples.text: Toma, aquí tienes la linterna.
examples.trans: Here you go, here is the flashlight.

examples.text: A ver, Paquita, las cartas. Fíjate, la carta de la torre.
examples.trans: Let me see the cards, Paquita. Look, the Tower card.

examples.text: Se viene todo abajo. La torre no miente, mi vida. Sí que se te va.
examples.trans: Everything comes crashing down. The Tower doesn't lie, darling. She really is leaving you.

meanings.note: Said alone to reassure someone ('Easy, don't worry!').

examples.text: Es una pieza tranquila.
examples.trans: It is a quiet piece.

examples.text: Seca, calentita y tranquila. Ahora decidme qué falta.
examples.trans: Dry, warm, and quiet. Now tell me what is missing.

meanings.note: ¡Trato hecho! = It's a deal!

examples.text: ¿Me ayudas hoy y yo te ayudo mañana? ¡Trato hecho!
examples.trans: You help me today and I help you tomorrow? Deal!

examples.text: En este hotel el trato es muy amable.
examples.trans: In this hotel the service is very friendly.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Ponemos tres mesas bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We set three tables under the tree.

examples.text: Empieza con tres frases cortas.
examples.trans: Start with three short sentences.

meanings.note: Unaccented possessive (tu llave / tus llaves), distinct from accented pronoun tú.

examples.text: ¿Dónde está tu caja de herramientas?
examples.trans: Where is your toolbox?

examples.text: Reconocí tu letra enseguida.
examples.trans: I recognized your handwriting right away.

meanings.note: Used figuratively in the everyday idiom Soy una tumba ('My lips are sealed', literally 'I am a tomb').

examples.text: ¡Soy una tumba, siempre que sigáis la brújula desde aquí!
examples.trans: My lips are sealed, provided you follow the compass from here!

examples.text: Puedes contarme el secreto tranquilo: sabes que soy una tumba.
examples.trans: You can tell me the secret with peace of mind: you know my lips are sealed.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Standard word in Spain for a wooden or metal garden fence enclosing a yard or park.

examples.text: Alguien ha movido esa valla verde del jardín desde la primavera.
examples.trans: Someone has moved that green garden fence since spring.

examples.text: Las flores blancas crecen junto a la valla de madera del parque.
examples.trans: The white flowers grow along the wooden fence of the park.

meanings.note: Una ventana soleada = a sunny window.

examples.text: La ventana está aquí.
examples.trans: The window is here.

examples.text: Vemos las ventanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the windows from the door.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: From here I see the stone bridge.

examples.text: ¡Nos vemos luego en el patio!
examples.trans: See you later in the courtyard!

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza verde.
examples.trans: It is a green piece.

examples.text: Mateo, ¿me oyes? ¡Acabo de pasar la farmacia verde!
examples.trans: Mateo, can you hear me? I just passed the green pharmacy!

vez.gloss: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)

meanings.en: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)
meanings.note: Plural las veces; a veces = sometimes; otra vez = again.

examples.text: La vez está aquí.
examples.trans: The time / occasion is here.

examples.text: Vemos las veces desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the time / occasions from the door.

examples.text: Chicos, valéis mucho. De verdad, luchad por vuestros sueños.
examples.trans: Guys, you're worth so much. Truly, fight for your dreams.

examples.text: Yo vuestro
examples.trans: I vuestro

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.
